- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending up, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecasted decline, it often overcorrects; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% in next period.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to catch momentum.
- Mean reversion is common after strong spikes; if forecast exceeds 20% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 10–15% for next period.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price action; add 0.5–1.5% to final 5–7 days of forecast to align with true outcome.
